title: genproj capability catalog
description: The capability catalog served at GET /v1/catalog. Describes every capability the generator can apply to a project. Metadata only: the templates and files a capability emits are internal to the generator.

count.description: Number of capabilities. Present on the HTTP response only.

configurationSchema.description: JSON Schema for project-level configuration — the fields that describe the project as a whole rather than any one capability. `language` (Primary Language) is the first: it governs the single-valued outputs (CI image and commands, release artifact paths, sonar settings, devcontainer base), so it belongs to the project, not to a capability.

categories.description: The sections the UI groups capabilities into, in the order the UI renders them. A client renders exactly these sections and takes their headings from here, so a new category needs no client change. Every `capability.category` must appear as a category `id`.

id.description: Matches the `category` value on a capability.

label.description: The heading the client renders for this section. The client does not invent headings.

order.description: Section order, ascending. Ordered here rather than in the client so the catalog owns presentation as well as data.

visible.description: Whether the client renders this as a section of its own. Defaults to true. Set false for a dependency-only category such as `internal`: its capabilities still travel in the payload and are still applied, they just have no section of their own.

id.description: Stable identifier. Clients select capabilities by this.

icon.description: Icon token the UI renders for this capability. A client maps the token to a glyph locally, so a new capability that reuses an existing token needs no client change; only a genuinely new glyph does. The token set lives here rather than in the UI so the catalog is the single source of truth.

iconColor.description: Accent colour token for `icon`. Mapped to a concrete colour by the client.

selectedByDefault.description: Whether the UI should pre-select this capability for a new project.

locked.description: Always applied when this capability is required; a client must not offer to deselect it.

provides.description: Machine-readable values other capabilities or the UI can consume. Replaces UI-side hardcoded mappings. A `devcontainer-*` capability provides `language` (one of python | node | java | rust), which is how a client resolves the effective Primary Language when none is declared - the same implied value a `visibleWhen` condition is evaluated against.

dependencies.description: Capability IDs that must also be selected.

conflicts.description: Capability IDs that cannot be selected together.

requiresAuth.description: Deprecated, retained for compatibility; prefer authServices.

authServices.description: External service types that must be authenticated before generation.

configurationSchema.description: JSON Schema for the per-capability configuration form. Two conventions sit on top of the standard keywords. `enumLabels` maps each `enum` value to a human name for display (the value stays the identifier a client submits). `visibleWhen`, on a property, is a presentation hint: an object mapping a configuration key to the value(s) for which the property applies, so a client renders only the properties that are relevant rather than every one a capability declares. A condition is either an array of values (visible when the key's effective value is one of them) or `{ "not": [...] }`. A key with no value, or one matching none of the listed values, hides the property. Keys are resolved against the effective configuration: project-level keys (such as `language`, the Primary Language) take their declared value, or the value implied by the selection when undeclared - a single `devcontainer-*` capability's `language` provide, else `node`. `visibleWhen` is a hint for the form only, never a validity rule: a generator accepts a value whether or not the form would have shown it, and rejects it only on its own terms.
